title: Reports
slide_intent: Teach how an identity can carry a reader between a report cover and an information-rich spread. These pages have different demands on attention and legibility.
strategic_value: Distinctive covers can help identify Frontline AIDS publications while recurring interior type and accent choices support longer reading.
demonstration: An array of angled covers and open reports sits on pink. Some lead with portraits, others with oversized illustration; the interiors show structured text, pictures and colored headings.
practical_value: Choose a cover treatment that names the report’s subject, then inspect an open spread to judge the relative space needed for text, evidence and photographs.

content_islands.name: Cover selection
content_islands.spec: Show multiple report fronts at the same angle so a reader can compare which asset leads each one.

content_islands.name: Interior spreads
content_islands.spec: Interleave open spreads among the covers and retain enough of each spread to show columns, inset images and typographic levels.
